reasons.claim: One eligible species is recorded within 250 m: the VU lichen Alectoria sarmentosa, at 200 m and 244 m (2022, uncertainty 25 m and 10 m). It is forest-associated and site-bound, and its threats include lack of continuity forest and of large or old trees.

Supporting records within 250 m are the site-bound NT lichens Lobaria pulmonaria (73 m, 2023) and Bryoria nadvornikiana (200 m, 2022). That makes 2, below the threshold of 3 for MEDIUM on NT species alone.

Mobile red-listed birds are recorded about 130-515 m away, including the VU Surnia ulula and the EN Aegolius funereus (2026). Their coordinate uncertainty is 390-500 m, and as mobile species they are supporting evidence only.
Effort is adequate (87 records, 60th percentile, county median 66). Near-site records: 3 inside the polygon and 18 within 250 m.
No completed felling overlaps the polygon. It is a 16.43 ha regeneration felling notification.

uncertainties: The Alectoria records are 200 m or more from the edge, so whether the species occupies the felling area is unknown.
Records are from 2022 or earlier for the key lichens, and the species may have changed since.
Coarse records were excluded near the site (5 inside, 41 within 250 m), so some nearby recordings may not be counted.
not_established: Presence or absence of red-listed species inside the polygon.
Stand age or quality; no tool output describes it.
That any species depends on the stand to be felled.
That the site is safe to fell.
next_action: Reviewer should do a field check of the stand for lichen habitat, in particular around the Alectoria sarmentosa, Lobaria pulmonaria and Bryoria nadvornikiana records 73-244 m away, before felling can begin.
